attempts.summary: Joined node2's and node3's separate segments (attached via node1's eth1 and eth2) into a single transparent L2 domain by building a kernel bridge (br0) on node1 (SONiC) spanning eth1/eth2, after neutralizing docker0's class-E IP leak and masking interfaces-config.service to prevent reconciliation conflicts. Assigned static IPs 192.168.50.11/24 (node2) and 192.168.50.12/24 (node3) on the same subnet via NetworkManager (autoconnect enabled for persistence). br0 carries no IP address, confirming node1 forwards frames at L2 rather than routing between the hosts. Verified direct reachability (ping/arping) and correct MAC learning in node1's bridge FDB for both peers. Persisted the bridge across reboot via a new systemd oneshot unit (l2-bridge.service, enabled at boot). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured healthy baselines, restarted node3, node2, and node1 one at a time using each node's native reboot mechanism, confirmed a changed boot_id on every node, and verified full recovery (bridge forwarding state, FDB relearning, SONiC's 9 containers healthy, and end-to-end L2 ping between node2 and node3) after each restart.
